title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 105
paragraphs: While Onesilus was besieging Amathus, it was reported to King Darius that Sardis had been captured and burned by the Athenians and the Ionians together, and that the leader of the conspiracy for bringing these things about was the Milesian Aristagoras. It is said that when he was first informed of this, he paid no heed to the Ionians, because he knew that they at any rate would not escape unpunished for their revolt, but he asked who the Athenians were; and when he had been told, he asked for his bow, and having received it and set an arrow on the string, he shot it up toward the heavens, and as he shot into the air he said: “Zeus, grant me to take vengeance on the Athenians!” Having so said, he charged one of his attendants to say to him, whenever dinner was set before the king, always three times: “Master, remember the Athenians.”
